items.title: CATL and Alfen ink 5GWh sodium-ion BESS deal for Europe
items.summary: CATL signed a memorandum of understanding with Dutch energy solutions provider Alfen to supply 5 gigawatt-hours of its newly launched sodium-ion TENER storage systems to western Europe, including the Netherlands, starting in 2027. The deal reflects CATL's dual-track strategy of advancing both lithium and sodium battery chemistries as it pushes into the European market.

items.title: NSW approves 3.6GWh Stratford Pumped Hydro and Solar project
items.summary: Gloucester Coal received planning approval from the New South Wales government for its 3.6GWh Stratford Pumped Hydro and Solar project, adding a major long-duration storage asset to the Australian pipeline. The approval comes amid a broader wave of grid-scale storage activity across the state.

items.title: Transgrid opens 900MW grid-forming battery pathway in NSW
items.summary: Australian transmission operator Transgrid has opened a pathway for 900MW of grid-forming inverter-equipped battery storage to help meet New South Wales' minimum system strength requirements. The move gives batteries a formal role in maintaining grid stability as more synchronous generation retires.

items.title: Global BESS additions hit 9.1GW/33.5GWh in one month
items.summary: New large-scale battery energy storage system data shows roughly 9.1GW and 33.5GWh came online globally last month, with Saudi Arabia accounting for over one-third of the total. The figures underline the Middle East's rapid emergence as a major storage deployment hub.

items.title: Tesla deploys 13.5GWh of energy storage in Q2 2026
items.summary: Tesla announced it deployed 13.5 GWh of energy storage capacity globally in Q2 2026, up 53% from Q1 and 40% higher than the same quarter last year. The figure represents the company's second-largest quarterly total on record, bringing cumulative deployments since 2016 past 132 GWh.

items.title: Scientists crack the code on solid-state battery dendrite failures
items.summary: Researchers have identified the mechanism by which soft lithium dendrites crack the hard ceramic electrolyte inside solid-state batteries, a process that triggers dangerous short circuits. The finding, published this month, could help engineers design safer, longer-lasting cells for EVs and grid storage.

items.title: Details emerge on CATL's zero-degradation BESS technology
items.summary: Industry analysts have published a deeper look at battery maker CATL's 'zero-degradation' BESS technology, first unveiled two years ago, examining how the claimed cycle-life and capacity-retention improvements hold up under real-world deployment conditions. The analysis comes as CATL simultaneously pushes sodium-ion products into new markets.

items.title: Peak Energy, ESS Tech and Unigrid advance sodium-ion storage
items.summary: Three companies made fresh announcements advancing sodium-ion energy storage technology across the US and Europe, part of a broader industry shift toward alternative chemistries. Peak Energy separately confirmed plans for a $71 million California factory dedicated to grid-scale sodium-ion systems, with shipments targeted for early 2027.

items.title: Elestor and Windpark Zeewolde deploy hydrogen-iron flow battery
items.summary: Dutch long-duration storage developer Elestor has partnered with Windpark Zeewolde to install a 20MW system with 200-800MWh capacity using hydrogen-iron flow battery technology at what is described as Europe's largest onshore wind farm. The project showcases growing momentum for long-duration alternatives to lithium-ion.

items.title: Moment Energy opens EV battery reuse megafactory in Vancouver
items.summary: Moment Energy has opened what it describes as the world's largest facility dedicated to repurposing retired EV batteries into modular energy storage systems for critical infrastructure. The Vancouver plant, called Megafactory 1, signals growing commercial traction for second-life battery technology.

items.title: Massachusetts launches consolidated BESS siting and permitting regime
items.summary: Massachusetts has launched a new consolidated siting and permitting framework specifically for battery storage projects, effective this month, aiming to streamline how facilities move from concept to construction. The reform is part of a broader wave of state-level regulatory changes designed to support continued BESS deployment.

items.title: OBBBA's FEOC rules reshape battery storage supply chains
items.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act preserved robust federal tax incentives for energy storage even as it pulled back support for wind and solar, but its strict new Foreign Entity of Concern requirements are forcing developers to rethink procurement strategies. Analysts note the law is simultaneously a tailwind and a supply-chain constraint for the BESS industry.

items.title: ISO-NE seeks delay in FERC large-load tariff proceeding
items.summary: ISO-NE and regional transmission owners have announced their intent to request a 90-day abeyance in FERC's large-load show-cause proceeding concerning tariff reforms for data centers and other large or co-located loads. The delay would allow additional stakeholder input ahead of a November 16, 2026 filing deadline.

items.title: Australia's AEMC weighs minimum system load rules for batteries
items.summary: Australia's Australian Energy Market Commission is consulting on minimum system load requirements in the National Electricity Market, with battery energy storage investment central to the debate. The outcome could shape how much flexibility grid operators require batteries to provide as renewable penetration grows.

items.title: Australia adds First Nations set-aside to storage tender rounds
items.summary: The Australian government has introduced a dedicated First Nations Set Aside pilot program into both Capacity Investment Scheme Tenders 9 and 10, aiming to boost Indigenous participation in the country's expanding battery storage procurement rounds. The move adds a new social-equity dimension to the national capacity investment framework.
